## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Enforce the five-attempt cap before merge. With the current default, an unavailable upstream receives ten requests from a single call.

## Changes

The pull request adds `fetch_with_retry`, which retries `OSError` with a configurable delay and defaults to ten attempts. It adds retry tests and a review fixture, and proposes raising the project’s retry cap to ten.

## Critical

- app/net.py:13 — correctness — Enforce the five-attempt retry cap — When `fetch(url)` raises `OSError` on every call, `fetch_with_retry(url)` makes ten attempts, and the guard also accepts explicit values from 6 through 10. `AGENTS.md:5` requires “Retry helpers under app/ must cap attempts at 5.” — During an upstream outage, each default call can send five additional requests beyond the project’s cap. — Fix: Set the default and maximum to five, then update the docstring and the tests for the default and upper boundary.

## Important

(none)

## Suggestions

- app/net.py:14 — comments — Specify which failures trigger a retry — If an upstream sends a malformed HTTP status line and `fetch` raises `BadStatusLine`, the helper exits on the first attempt. The docstring says “Call fetch until it succeeds or attempts calls have failed,” but the handler is `except OSError:`. — Callers relying on the documented retry behavior can get an exception on the first attempt after a malformed response.
- app/net.py:27 — tests — Assert the configured delay before retrying — For `delay=0.25` and a first attempt that raises `OSError`, the tests would pass if the helper retried immediately. Every multi-attempt test replaces `sleep` with a no-op that records no calls. — A regression that drops or ignores the configured delay can go undetected. — Fix: Extend `test_fetch_with_retry_succeeds_after_failures` to check the configured delay.
